sections.what: Tells Next.js to build a fully static website into plain files, skip image optimisation, add a trailing slash to addresses, and place the whole site under a subfolder path. The same subfolder path is made available to browser code.

summary: Configures Next.js to build a fully static website and sets the subfolder path the site is served under.
purpose: Tells the build how to produce plain files, which address prefix to use, and how image handling works.
why: Likely reason: the site is hosted as static files under a subfolder, such as a GitHub Pages project site. Reason not stated in the code.
how: Sets the subfolder path once, then turns on static export, turns off image optimisation, adds a trailing slash to addresses, and passes the subfolder path to browser code.
inputs: Read by Next.js when the site is built or run.
outputs: Changes how the site is built, including where links point and how images are handled.
risks: The subfolder path must match the real hosting address, or every link and image breaks. Static export disables features that need a server.
debug: If links or images are broken on the live site, compare the subfolder path with the hosting address. If the build output looks wrong, check the export setting.
